reviews.title: Amazing case!
reviews.comment: I got this to replace my Be Quiet Pure Base 500 FX so that I could accommodate a new 360mm AIO (Also Be Quiet) and a larger GPU. This is one of the easiest cases I have ever built in. Moving everything over went smoothly. The built in fan/ RBG hubs made wiring those a breeze. My PC is beautiful now. Can't wait for my new GPU to get here on Friday. Temps have been fantastic so far.

reviews.title: Great Case, with some Quirks
reviews.comment: Picked this up during Amazon Prime Days. This case seems like is a premium, quiet mid-tower with a clean design, good airflow, and solid materials.  setup experience might not be so  smooth, especially for first-time or occasional builders. The case itself is great: very sturdy construction, thick steel panels, quality Silent fans pre-installed, and plenty of room inside for a full-size GPU and 360mm AIO. I had issues with sliding the back vented panel off: it was very stuck to the point where I thought I’d need a pry bar (or return it for replacement) but eventually came off. I had no issues fitting an RTX 4080 and a front-mounted 360mm AIO cooler. Cable management is great with lots of room behind the motherboard tray, zip ties, and rubber grommets. Where it falls short is the documentation. The included manual is your typical Chinese pictograms; very basic. Not all cables are labeled, and there’s no clear diagram showing where everything is inside the case. If you’re a beginner, this could definitely slow you down or leave you guessing what goes where. A simple labeled diagram or cable map would have made a huge difference. SSDs are to be installed along the “door” of the back of the case. However, the provided screws will not work with the smaller holes of SSDs. With the rubber standoff grommets provided, no screws will work. The RGB lighting is minimal but tasteful — just a front strip with motherboard sync support or using the dedicated button on the front case controls. If you’re into subtle lighting, this fits the aesthetic perfectly. Airflow is solid out of the box, and with one extra fan for exhaust, temps stayed excellent while still whisper-quiet. Pros: • Very quiet, even under load • Nice build quality with a clean, minimal look • Spacious interior with great cable routing • DX ARGB fans included • Good airflow and support for large GPUs/AIOs Cons: • Poor documentation and unlabeled cables • Not very beginner-friendly • Need to unstick the sliding back panel • Screws for SSD installation or improved mounting. Bottom Line: If you’re an experienced builder or willing to take your time, the 600 LX is a great case. It runs cool and quiet and looks premium without going over the top. But if you’re new to PC building, be prepared to do some trial-and-error or look up extra help online, because the instructions definitely leave something to be desired.
